subject: Executive recap: outcomes, decision criteria, and procurement checkpoints for ClearMind POC

Subject: Follow-up + executive recap request — Redwood POC next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for a productive conversation earlier. Quick recap from our side to ensure executive alignment and make procurement straightforward: 

1) Primary business outcomes you shared
- Reduce customer support L1 handle time by ~40% for knowledge-base driven tickets 
- Deflect 20% of chat volume through a high-precision assistant trained on internal KB

2) Key constraints and risks you flagged
- Data residency: production inference must remain in the US (no EU replication)
- SOC 2 evidence is required for pilot start (controls + encryption at rest)
- Peak latency target: 300ms p95 for short-turn queries (10–50 tokens)

3) Proposed path & near-term asks
- Redwood provides a 6-week proof-of-concept using a dedicated instance (sandbox subnet in your VPC)
- We’ll deliver a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones: infra runway, integration checklist, success metrics, go/no-go decision date
- Can ClearMind confirm procurement owner and any PO/contracting timing constraints?

I attached a one-pager (redwood-onepager.pdf) and a draft MAP (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) for your review.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll prepare a short executive brief you can share with your CIO/Head of Product.
- Marissa will own the SOC 2 paperwork and initial security checklist.

Could you confirm: who at ClearMind approves the technical POC scope and who owns contracting? Also, what is your target decision window (we discussed mid-November)?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Subject: Exec recap & action checklist for ClearMind pilot (for leadership)

Marissa / Karthik —

Summary for leadership share: please feel free to forward this language to our sales leadership or the product ops review. I’m keeping the tone exec-friendly with clear asks.

TL;DR- ClearMind wants a 6-week POC to validate L1 deflection and latency targets; decision window: mid-November. Procurement can turn a PO in ~1–2 weeks if we provide SOC 2 evidence + draft SOW by 29 Oct.

Business outcomes (as stated by ClearMind execs)
- 40% reduction in L1 handle time across KB-driven issues
- 20% chat deflection target (accuracy > 85% on KB answers)

Open risks and mitigation
- SOC 2: Marissa to provide controls summary and auditor contact. If full Type II not available, provide interim evidence and compensate with additional monitoring and audit hooks.
- Data residency: must host POC in their US-only VPC. Karthik, we should confirm network setup and whether we need an on-prem appliance for the KV cache.
- Latency: target p95 <= 300ms. Offer: can provision a smaller dedicated GPU pool + autoscaling floor for the pilot to meet targets; include fallback plan to model-short-circuit to a lighter quantized variant if latency breaches for >30 minutes.

Procurement ask (by Thu EOD 29 Oct) - SOC 2 evidence bundle - Draft SOW (milestones & invoice split) - Security appendix & DPA

Owner matrix
- SOC 2 / security pack: Marissa Co-lead (owner)
- SOW & pricing: Jonas (owner)
- Network / infra setup: Karthik (owner)

Immediate next steps I’ll execute today:
1) Send SOC 2 summary and controls contact (Marissa: if you can confirm the file I’ll forward)
2) Draft SOW template with 30/30/40 milestone schedule and include the latency fallback clause
3) Share a short one-page exec brief formatted for Avery Lin and the CIO (Elena asked for something concise)

Questions for leadership (quick)
- Do we want to offer a 7-day SLA credit for pilot latency breaches to reduce procurement friction?
- Any constraints on committing a dedicated sandbox inside a customer-managed VPC? (If yes, escalate to infra ops.)

Please add anything I missed. If not, I’ll get the SOW + SOC bundle in Tom’s hands before EOD Thu.

Thanks,
Jonas
